question.problem: Expressed as a fraction in its simplest form, $\sqrt{\frac{4}{25}}=${{field-1}}.
question.worked_solution:
Recall that if $a\ge 0,$ then

$$
\sqrt{{a}^{2}}=a.
$$

First, notice that $4$ and $25$ are both perfect squares, where

$$
4={2}^{2},
$$

and

$$
25={5}^{2}.
$$

So, to work out $\sqrt{\frac{4}{25}},$ we express $\frac{4}{25}$ as a perfect square:

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt{\frac{4}{25}} & = \\ \sqrt{\frac{{2}^{2}}{{5}^{2}}} & = \\ \sqrt{\frac{2\cdot 2}{5\cdot 5}} & = \\ \sqrt{\frac{2}{5}\cdot \frac{2}{5}} & = \\ \sqrt{{(\frac{2}{5})}^{2}} & = \\ \frac{2}{5} & \end{aligned}
$$
